newsitem.title: UK: British driver accused of murdering French student.
newsitem.headline: British driver accused of murdering French student.

text.p: A British truck driver accused of killing a 19-year-old French student kept her body in his cab for 10 days and gave away some of her possessions as Christmas presents, a court was told on Wednesday.
Stuart Morgan, 37, has admitted that he gave 19-year-old Celine Figard, a fluent English speaker, a lift in his truck last December, but he denies raping and strangling her.

"We say that he raped her and killed her in the back of his lorry in the late afternoon or early evening of 19 December within quite a short time of picking her up," prosecuting lawyer David Farrer told the court in Worcester central England.

"We say that he kept her body hidden behind the driving seat of his lorry for very nearly 10 days over the whole of the Christmas period. During that time he drove considerable distances with the body lying behind him."

Figard was last seen alive at a service area on a motorway near the town of Newbury, southern England. Ten days later police found her naked, bruised body 90 miles (144.8 km) away in woods near a main road at Hawford in the English Midlands.
She had been strangled and beaten around the head and marks on her wrists indicated she had been bound up.

Morgan, from Parkstone, southern England, quietly took notes in court as the jury of nine women and three men heard on the opening day how Figard went missing as she hitch-hiked through England to meet her cousin at the hotel where he worked.
Figard's parents were also in the courtroom, listening to a translation of the proceedings through headphones.
Morgan has admitted he had sexual intercourse with Figard, but he says she consented and that he later dropped her off at the roadside.

Farrer told the court that shortly after the accountancy student's death, Morgan made Christmas gifts of two bottles of champagne that Figard had been given by a vineyard owner who does not export his produce to Britain.
The prosecutor said the cab of Morgan's white truck was splashed with blood, which DNA tests showed belonged to Figard.

A blood-stained mattress from one of the bunk beds in the cab of the truck was found in Morgan's garage and clothes belonging to Figard were found at a warehouse that Morgan had visited in the days after her death.

Farrer also accused Morgan, who was arrested and charged with the murder in February, of changing the tachograph on his truck to cover up any record of the trip. This was a case of "calculating and unmitigating wickedness", said Farrer.
The trial is expected to last two weeks.
